chapter: Ann Cook session and Buddy Petit stories
title: Baseball park gig and the train trip with Buddy Petit
summary: Humphrey tells of playing for a colored baseball park, then the train ride with Buddy Petit, who stopped over and met Baptiste.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I mean, the Fritz is, you know, better than heading around here. So a buddy decided he wanted to come back there, well we was playing up at the B. St. Park up there. We had that sold up. Which park? B. St. Park. Baseball park up there. Claybone and uh... That's part of the Claybone car went. Let me see now, do you recall that? No, Palm there? No. No. It was in Jefferson Parish when you book stuff. But see that there's a된 baseball park there. Peace out, Paul. No, it was in Jefferson Parish when you approached that aluminum place up there. See that's a good baseball park.
South Claiborne in Mississippi I reckon. I think that street must be Mississippi Street.
It's well past Carrollton then huh? Oh yeah. Long past Carrollton. I got to fix it all right.

Go right to the South Claiborne course, that's where it went. At that time that was the Orleans and the Jefferson Parish line. Canal. I think it's called Mississippi Street. Well that park was on that side. Colored park. Baseball park. All the college, you know, colored college. Had the football game and everything up there. Well, now we played for that. You hide a park, you hide a bag. stuff at him. But he drank plenty. He spent, he stripped it, you know, the same as I am, man. Got nothing else, man. So we got on that train, you know. They didn't buy no ticket, you know. The man come through there and buy a ticket. But now, the train, back to back there, the police say, man, get in there. We ain't got no, we ain't gonna bootleg you any time. And he's a little fella, you know. Buddy got in between them, that seat back up there. That's the other seat. But we get, man, I'll take it. And look at Buddy in there. He sit back there, in that corner, just drive down in there. Brought him in the yard. Well, of course, if the man saw me, that'd pay for him, you know. First baby stop at 25. That was very moray. 25? Yeah. I think it was very moray at 25, wasn't it? No, that was 25 was at, at, at,
at, at, uh, Abbeville and Franklin, customized in Franklin. Yeah. Well, anyhow, that's where

we stopped at. But he know he had, he know he had friends there, see. Yeah. I walked over there. And, uh, Baptiste was there. What is Baptiste? He was a gambler, trumpet player. He told, uh, Baptiste said, what you gonna do today? I said, well, Baptiste used to take lessons from him. You know what I mean. Father, he's a great father of Buddy Petit. Mm-hmm. I'll call you home. You dig.

I asked him, say, where you gonna sleep at? Well, I bet he had a rooming house down the street. But he said, I ain't got nowhere to play, I ain't going home. And that's going, what time you got a play? Well, we supposed to start that appetite in that day at one o'clock. It was about nine o'clock then. And, uh, boy went and took him a nap and everything, you know. He had the horn with him, he got that horn. And we gonna meet, uh, Third and Willa, baseball players and all, you know, make a little appetizer and all.
